outcome: composite severe neonatal morbidity (assisted ventilation > 6 hours, neonatal seizures, Apgar score < 4 at 5 minutes)
cohort: The study population included 531,440 full term, singleton, cephalic vaginal births among individuals with a previous cesarean birth in the United States.
finding: Rates of severe neonatal morbidity are higher following operative vaginal births compared to spontaneous vaginal births; while no statistically significant difference was found in overall severe neonatal morbidity between forceps and vacuum births, forceps births showed a 39% higher odds of assisted ventilation > 6 hours.
mod_finding: Rates of severe neonatal morbidity are higher following operative vaginal births (forceps or vacuum) compared to spontaneous vaginal births, with forceps births showing a higher odds of assisted ventilation > 6 hours compared to vacuum births.
